newsitem.title: UK: Air Foyle cashes in on Spain lorry drivers' strike.
newsitem.headline: Air Foyle cashes in on Spain lorry drivers' strike.

text.p: UK cargo airline Air Foyle said it has earned revenues approaching 200,000 stg from operating Valencia-London Luton IL-76 charter flights for customers hit by the 12-day-old Spanish lorry drivers' strike.
"We have flown six of these flights over the past two weeks, carrying mainly car engines and parts manufactured in Spain for assembly in the UK," said Air Foyle marketing spokeswoman Claire Mundy.
"The main customers have been Vauxhall and Ford and the weight of loads has ranged from 10 tonnes per flight to the IL-76's maximum 40 tonnes' payload," she told Reuters.
She added that requests for ex-Spain charter flight quotations started to come in as soon as reports that the truckers' strike was a possibility earlier this month.

"We operated similar flights from the Continent to the UK last November to bypass the French lorry drivers' strike. At that time, many customers left their flight bookings until the last minute, but this time they were prepared," said Mundy.
Customers during the French strike, she said, included Volvo and Rover.
"We have no further firm bookings for Spain-UK charters resulting from the Spanish strike but these tend to come in on a morning requesting a flight the same day," she added.
